learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to provide an in-depth understanding of heat transfer mechanisms (conduction, convection, and radiation) and their applications in engineering contexts.
Students will be able to apply the acquired knowledge to analyze and design thermal systems, evaluate energy performance, and optimize solutions based on specific requirements.
Develop the ability to interpret thermal data and make informed design decisions, taking into account technical, economic, and environmental aspects.
Be able to effectively communicate the results of thermal analyses and design solutions, both in written and oral form, using appropriate technical terminology.
Acquire the necessary skills to independently deepen advanced topics in the field of heat transfer and to pursue further studies or professional activities in the energy sector.

syllabus_topics: REVIEW OF HEAT TRANSFER MECHANISMS: CONDUCTION, CONVECTION, AND RADIATION (9 H)
DIMENSIONLESS NUMBERS FOR HEAT TRANSFER (2 H)
EVALUATION OF CONVECTIVE HEAT TRANSFER COEFFICIENTS: THEORETICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES (4 H)
HEAT EXCHANGERS: TYPES, PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS, APPLICATIONS (2 H)
DESIGN AND OPTIMIZATION OF HEAT EXCHANGERS (NTU METHOD, CFD) (8 H)
INDUSTRIAL HEAT RECOVERY AND THERMAL ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS (INCLUDING PHASE CHANGE MATERIALS) (6 H)
COOLING OF NEXT-GENERATION ELECTRONIC COMPONENTS (5 H)
PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: DESIGN OF THERMAL SYSTEMS, SOFTWARE SIMULATION (20 H)
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by the project evaluation (70%) and the oral exam (30%). The project report must be submitted at least five days before the oral exam and has a minimum passing score of 20 points out of 30. The oral exam consists of two theoretical questions and requires a minimum passing score of 14 points out of 17. A passing level for the oral exam demonstrates the ability to identify methodological tools, properly set up the problem, and indicate viable solutions.

INCROPERA ET AL., FUNDAMENTALS OF HEAT AND MASS TRANSFER, WILEY
